Subject: GenomicAI kickoff: multipool needs and regional questions

Sean —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to get the ball rolling for a Dedicated pool setup for our inference workloads. A few constraints and asks from our side:

- Primary regions: us-west-2 and us-east-1. We need local inference for latency-sensitive customers.
- Baseline traffic: ~180 concurrent sessions (avg inference size 512 tokens) during peak window.
- Cold start tolerance: we can tolerate 150–200ms cold-start spikes but want 95th pct under 120ms after warmups.
- Burst profile: spikes up to ~2.2x baseline for sustained 20–40 minute windows during nightly batch processes.
- Compliance: SOC2 attestation required for audit before EOY; if you have a checklist, please send.
- PO and signed SOW inbound — procurement will send PO this week (attaching an outline of expected payment schedule).

Can we align on a short kickoff next Tue or Wed? Also looking for an initial runbook / provisioning template you recommend for multipool setups.

Thanks,
Dave
Ops Lead, GenomicAI

Dave — thanks, this is great context and helps scope the first pass. Confirming availability: Tue 2026-11-10 10:00 PT or Wed 2026-11-11 11:00 PT — let me know what works for your ops and infra folks.

High-level proposal for kickoff agenda (30–45m):
- Introductions + success criteria (5m)
- Topology proposal: 2-region multipool (primary us-west-2, secondary us-east-1) + cross-region failover (10m)
- Autoscale & burst policy suggestions tied to your traffic profile (10m)
- Activation plan & timeline: provisioning, smoke tests, canary routing (10m)
- Action items & owners (5m)

I attached a lightweight starter config (initial_pool_config.yaml) and a capacity planning workbook stub — we can iterate on numbers during the call. Key suggestions up front:
- Reserved baseline: provision capacity to cover ~1.2x baseline (so reserve for ~220 concurrent sessions across pools) to reduce immediate cold-starts.
- Autoscale: aggressive scale-up threshold (70% GPU util sustained for 30s) + staged burst headroom (allow burst to 1.5x reserved automatically; manual escalation to 2.2x with capacity owner approval).
- Fall-back policy: when cross-region latency is acceptable (<35ms increase), route non-latency-critical requests to secondary. For critical traffic, prefer local routing with degraded response when under-provisioned.

Proposed owners for the call: Sean (SE lead / kickoff), Karthik (capacity ops / autoscale config), Marissa (CS lead for implementation), Monica (PO & SOW handoff).

Please confirm a time and we’ll send an invite with a focused pre-read.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

All — quick ops notes after reviewing Dave's workbook (thanks for the upload):

- Suggested pool shapes: mix of 8xA100-80GB for baseline (model size dependent) and a smaller fleet of cheaper T4-equivalents for non-critical batch jobs.
- Baseline math: to hit ~220 concurrent sessions (avg token length 512) with <120ms p95, initial reserved = 10 A100s across the two regions (split 6 / 4). Reserve slightly more in us-west-2.
- Burst policy (proposal):
  - min_capacity: 4 GPUs (keep cost floor)
  - reserved_capacity: 10 GPUs (covers steady state + buffer)
  - autoscale_headroom: allow auto-scale up to reserved_capacity * 1.5 (15 GPUs) based on util triggers
  - manual_burst_override: ops can open manual bursting up to 22 GPUs (2.2x) for up to 60 minutes; we enforce cooldown 30m after manual burst
- Cache/warmup: enable prefix caching for top 20% of requests (based on historical keys) and pre-warm heavy models during known batch windows to reduce cold-starts.
- Monitoring: wire in token-level cost & latency dashboards, set alert if p95 latency > 140ms or autoscale > 80% of max headroom for 10 minutes.
- Failover: prefer active-active routing for read-only endpoints; for strict consistency endpoints we recommend active-passive with health checks and a 60s failover guard.

I attached a sample YAML (initial_pool_config.yaml) with the above knobs. Marissa / Monica — during the kickoff I'll show the dashboard views to confirm SLOs and alerts.

-Karthik
Capacity Operations Lead | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: initial_pool_config.yaml (yaml)]
